title: SDK Resilience Playbook: error semantics, recovery snippets, and cross-language patterns
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Summary:
Create a developer-facing "playbook" and reference implementation that standardizes SDK error semantics, retry/backoff defaults, streaming resume ergonomics, and actionable error messages across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs. The artifact should include canonical exception classes, stable error code strings, recommended retry strategies for transient vs terminal failures, resumable-stream contract and example snippets, and migration notes for existing clients.

Goals:
- Reduce user confusion when clients see different errors across languages.
- Provide clear, actionable remediation text in errors (e.g., "increase timeout", "enable idempotency token", "retry with exponential backoff"), not just opaque codes.
- Define telemetry tags and linkable remediation IDs so support can map errors to runbook pages and incident reports.
- Offer battery of small, copy-paste examples for each language that show best-practices for retries and stream reconnection.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: changing server-side error formats or API surface. Focus is on SDK surface and guidance.

Deliverables:
1) Playbook doc that becomes a living page in our SDK docs site.
2) Reference PRs for Python/TS/Go adding new exception classes and helpers, plus example snippets.
3) Unit + integration test plans that validate retry semantics and resume tokens under fault injection.
4) Migration notes and changelog entries for next SDK releases.
comments: 2026-03-10: Aisha opened the ticket, initial outline in description. Suggested pairing with observability team for telemetry keys.
2026-03-11: Jonas: scoped deliverables and estimate; flagged dependency on ENG-220401 (stream resume flow).
2026-03-12: Design note from Priya Desai (SDK lead): prefer explicit RetryableError/TransientError base classes rather than boolean flags on exceptions to improve type safety in TypeScript and Go.

2026-03-12: Engineering discussion: agreed default client retry policy should be a conservative exponential backoff with jitter, max attempts 4, default idempotency opt-in for non-streaming calls. Add opt-out for strict latency-sensitive code paths.
2026-03-13: Security: flagged that error messages must not include PII or KMS key identifiers. Security review required: false (security already consulted informally).
2026-03-13: Jonas: added acceptance criteria and sample snippet drafts. Will open language-specific PRs after doc review.
2026-03-13: Follow-up: coordinate with Docs (Emily Chen) for canonical page and example formatting.
acceptance_criteria: Doc page published under SDK docs with examples for Python/TS/Go
Each SDK exposes canonical exception hierarchy or error types with stable error_code property strings
Retry helpers implemented in each SDK honoring recommended defaults and allowing opt-out/configuration
Streaming client supports a documented resume contract and illustrative reconnection snippet in each language
Unit/integration tests cover injected transient errors and confirm backoff behavior
Changelog entries and migration notes available for upcoming releases
test_plan: Unit tests: raise transient and terminal errors and assert retry helper behavior. Integration: run fault-injection harness against staging runtime to simulate capacity throttling and intermittent connection drops, verify resume token logic and telemetry tags emitted. Manual QA: docs walkthrough and code snippet verification in sample apps.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge docs and reference PRs to main branches behind feature flags. 2) Publish SDK patch releases with opt-in flags. 3) After 2 weeks of telemetry review, flip defaults for new retry helpers if metrics look good. 4) Announce in changelog and migration guide.
